5.text: In religious beliefs and rites the dog plays a more important part than

6.text: the reindeer, though, under the present condition of life, dogs are of little

7.text: use to the people; besides, dog-breeding does not harmonize well with reindeer-

8.text: breeding, as will be shown later on. I was told several times by the Reindeer

9.text: people, “The Russians unjustly wonder why we keep so many dogs. The

10.text: dog is the guardian of man, a strong help in every misfortune, a true friend,

11.text: keeping off the Evil One.” In travelling, a dog as a companion frightens

12.text: the evil spirit away, while a reindeer has no such power. In times of infectious

13.text: disease a small pup is rubbed against visitors coming from afar. This will

14.text: either frighten away the spirits that may come with the traveller, or, if they

15.text: are too powerful, it will at least serve as an expiatory victim.

16.text: On the other hand, the names of the months, both in Chukchee and in

17.text: Koryak, curiously enough, indicate that both of these tribes, or some parts

18.text: of them, came from more southern latitudes, and that perhaps they had

19.text: reindeer-herds at that time. The fact is, that some of these names do not

20.text: correspond to the real change of the seasons on the northern tundra. For

21.text: instance, the fifth month of the Chukchee year (from the beginning of April

22.text: to the beginning of May) is called “[month] of the waters” (Imlɪˊrɪlɪn). The

30.text: Another curious detail in the Chukchee tradition points even farther to

31.text: the south. It is the description of a large worm that lives near the villages

32.text: of the dead, on the Aurora Borealis. This worm is red in color, and striped,

33.text: and is so large that it can attack big game. When hungry, it is very active,

34.text: and will spring from ambush upon a wild reindeer, and then, after having

35.text: seized it, will kill it with the pressure of its coils. It swallows its prey whole,

36.text: since it has no teeth. After taking a meal, it becomes inert, and sleeps for
